info.description: File-scoped, queryable design-change API. Errors are RFC 9457 problem details with `code` and `hint`.

patch.description: Changes a tracked file's settings; returns the file with every setting (defaults filled in). Agent tokens and agent portal sessions only (viewers get wrong_token_class). `trackLibraryComponents` (default true): false stops tracking library (remote) components — the plugin stops scanning library mains at its next sync, and stored library nodes drop out of listings, summaries, counts, work-item progress and trends (nothing is deleted; true restores them). Instances of library components stay tracked; with `expand=instances` their mains appear as `kind: "library"` reference items. `storeImages` (default true): false refuses every image upload for the file (note screenshots, screen references, render-check results) with images_disabled. Render checks: `autoTargets` (default true) detects check targets in checked scopes (set_scope_checks); `variantMappings`, `themeMode` / `themeKey` and `gallery` say how targets render; `checkRetention` (default 5) results are kept per target. `gallery` and `variantMappings` are replaced whole. Unknown settings are invalid_parameter. Emits `file.settings_changed` (`data.settings`) when a setting changes; its actor is the body's `worker` when given, `portal:<label>` on a session-authenticated call, else the token label.

get.description: Nodes of a file with their property-level changes — by default the dirty ones (design changed since last built), compact, in document order (the design's layer order), 100 per page. The main read for implementation work: filter by subtree (`under` — one node id or several comma-separated — or a `url` with node-id), type, change, category, component or name; values within a parameter are OR, parameters are AND. Each node's `changes` is `{ prop: { built, now } }` and `contentHash` is what `clear_nodes` needs. For counts only use `summarize`; to work component by component use `list_work_items`. Every node carries `changedProps` and, for instances, `isInstance` / `mainComponentId` (`instance=true` lists only instances). By default (`changes=auto`) `added` nodes have no `changes` — on a fresh sync every node is added, so pages stay small; get their values with `changes=diff`, `view=full` or `get_node`. Change values over 1 KB are replaced by `{ truncated: true, bytes }` and the page has `truncated: true`; `view=full` or `get_node` returns them whole. `expand=instances` returns everything a screen uses in one call: with `under` = the screen, it adds the main components its instances point at (and theirs, transitively), each once; filters apply to that union (`expand=instances&state=dirty` = every dirty node the screen uses). Scope nodes come first, then each component in discovery order; expanded nodes carry `via` (the instance that reached them), and `expansion` reports the count, `truncated` and `unresolved` (unsynced) components. Page with `nextCursor` → `cursor`. On `unknown_parameter` / `invalid_parameter` follow `hint`; on `invalid_cursor` keep every other parameter unchanged or drop `cursor`.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Comma-separated: dirty, clean, blocked, requested, all. Default dirty (changed since last built or with open notes, not blocked); `requested`: dirty only by open notes; `all` for every state.

parameters.name: under
parameters.description: Only this node's subtree, the node included (1:2 or 1-2). Several subtrees: up to 50 comma-separated ids (1:2,1:5) for their union, each node once, in the order given. Defaults to the `url` link's node-id.

parameters.name: depth
parameters.description: Needs `under`: at most this many levels below it — below each root when there are several (1 = direct children).

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Comma-separated Figma node types, e.g. TEXT,INSTANCE,FRAME.

parameters.name: changeType
parameters.description: Comma-separated: added, modified, deleted, requested (dirty nodes only; `requested`: built as designed but with open notes).

parameters.name: hasNotes
parameters.description: true: only nodes with open notes; false: only nodes without.

parameters.name: changed
parameters.description: Comma-separated changed property names (fills, paddingLeft); a trailing `*` matches a prefix (padding*).

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Comma-separated change categories: layout, color, typography, effects, component, content, structure, prototype, token, other, note, render.

parameters.name: component
parameters.description: Comma-separated main component ids: the components and all their instances.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Comma-separated case-insensitive name globs (`*`, `?`), e.g. Button*.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: ISO 8601 time: only nodes changed at or after it.

parameters.name: claimed
parameters.description: Comma-separated: true (leased), false (free), mine (leased to `worker`).

parameters.name: worker
parameters.description: Your worker id; needed with `claimed=mine`.

parameters.name: instance
parameters.description: true: only component instances (`isInstance`); false: only other nodes.

parameters.name: library
parameters.description: Library nodes (remote main components / sets and their layers): include, exclude, or only them. Default: include when the file tracks library components (`settings.trackLibraryComponents`), else exclude.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: All the filters above in one string: space-separated `key:value` pairs, e.g. `state:dirty under:1:2 changed:fills` (several subtrees: `under:1:2,1:5`); quote values with spaces (name:"Primary Button"). A key may not also be passed as its own parameter.

parameters.name: view
parameters.description: compact (default: state, changes, hash, claim, block) or full (adds attrs, implementedAttrs, path; change values never truncated).

parameters.name: changes
parameters.description: auto (default): the built→now diff for modified and deleted nodes, omitted for added ones (their property names are in `changedProps`) — keeps fresh-sync pages small; diff: the diff for every node, including added ones' full values; names: never `changes`, only `changedProps`. Ask for `changes=diff` (or `get_node`) when you need the values of added nodes.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Comma-separated node fields to return (overrides view): nodeId, name, type, parentId, isInstance, mainComponentId, component, state, changeType, changedProps, changes, changesKnown, contentHash, figmaUrl, library, claim, blocked, notes, screen, attrs, implementedAttrs, path, deleted, notesResolved, history, descendants, usage, via (`via` needs `expand=instances`).

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Comma-separated: counts, usage. `counts` adds subtree counts (`descendants`) to each node; `usage` adds `usage: { layers }` to each design token (`token:<variableKey>`).

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: document (default: the design's layer order — auto-layout flow order, else top-to-bottom, left-to-right), path (node-id path order), updatedAt or name; prefix `-` for descending.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size (default 100, max 1000). With format=outline: rendered lines per page (default: every line).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The previous page's `nextCursor`, unchanged, with all other parameters the same (else `invalid_cursor`). With format=outline: the previous response's `X-RDS-Next-Cursor` header (a line position in the rendered outline).

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: A Figma link (figma.com/design/<fileKey>/…?node-id=1-2). Supplies the path parameters given as '-'; on routes with `under`, its node-id is the default `under`.

parameters.name: expand
parameters.description: `instances`: also include the subtree of every main component the scope's instances use (the scope is `under`, or the whole file) — transitively through instances inside those components, breadth-first, each component once. Use it for "everything this screen uses" / "which components do I build for this screen". Other filters apply after expansion; `depth` cannot be combined with it.

parameters.name: expandDepth
parameters.description: With `expand=instances`: at most this many instance → main hops (default 10, max 20; 1 = only the components the scope uses directly).

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: json (default); ndjson — one JSON object per line, streamed; md — a markdown checklist, one line per row, streamed. ndjson and md return every match from `cursor` on (up to `limit` when given) instead of one page. outline — text/plain, an indented tree with one line per node: use this first to see a screen's structure (under=<the screen>, and expand=instances for the components inside). Line: `Name (TYPE) · added` — `clean`, `added`, `deleted`, or `modified (3: fills, paddingLeft, …)` (changed property count and the first names), `· blocked` when blocked; an instance shows `(INSTANCE → <mainComponentId> <main name>)`. Two spaces per level of the tree below `under` (the `under` node itself, when it matches, is at the left margin; with several `under` ids, the tree of each root follows that of the previous root, in the order given, each root at the left margin). A node whose ancestors the filters leave out is indented under its nearest shown ancestor (at the margin when none is shown) — no placeholder lines. With expand=instances, a component's subtree is nested, as `↳ Name (COMPONENT) · …`, under the first instance that reached it; other instances of it show `→ <mainComponentId> (shown above)` (or `(shown below)`). Always in document order (the design's layer order; `sort=path` for node-id path order); nodes positioned absolutely in an auto-layout parent are marked `(absolute)`. Lines are the `fields`-independent summary. The whole result (up to 2000 rows, in order) is rendered once, then paged by rendered lines, so nesting and `(shown above)` read the same at any page size: `limit` is lines per page (default: every line), and when lines remain the response has an `X-RDS-Next-Cursor` header — pass it as `cursor`, with every other parameter unchanged, for the next lines. Past the 2000-row cap the outline's last line (counted like any other) is `… N more (use cursor/limit) — cursor=<c>` (the same cursor is in the header), which continues after the rendered part.

isInstance.description: An INSTANCE of a component; `mainComponentId` is that component.

mainComponentId.description: The instance's main component node id (`get_node` it, or filter `component=`); null for non-instances.

component.description: The captured component reference (the main for an instance, self for a component), including its set when it is a variant; null on other nodes.

set.description: The variant's Figma component set. Omitted when unavailable (including inaccessible library parents).

changedProps.description: Sorted names of the properties changed since last built (every property of an `added` node).

changes.description: Property-level diff against what was built: `{ prop: { built, now, category } }`; values bound to a token are `{ token, value }`. `null` when unknown (`changesKnown: false`). Omitted for `added` nodes by default (`changes=auto`) and always with `changes=names`. In compact listing / work responses a side whose JSON exceeds 1 KB is `{ truncated: true, bytes }` — `get_node` returns it whole.

figmaUrl.description: The node in Figma. For a library node: the main component in its library file, or null while unresolved (see `library`).

library.description: Library nodes only (null on others): a remote (library) main component or component set, or a layer inside one. `key` is its component key (the nearest component's); `resolved` is true when the server (RDS_FIGMA_TOKEN) has resolved it to the library file — then `fileKey` is that file and `figmaUrl` opens the component there. Unresolved: `figmaUrl` is null; find it in the library by `key`.

notes.description: Open notes, newest first: what a person or agent says does not match the design. Read them, fix the code to match the design as they describe, then clear the node — clearing resolves them. A node with open notes is dirty (`changeType: requested` when its design is otherwise built).

source.description: Only when not a person's note: `render_check` (a failed render check; its screenshots show the difference).

items.description: A stored image. `url` / `thumbUrl` need the same bearer token or portal session as the API (get_attachment).

url.description: API path of the full image.

thumbUrl.description: API path of the thumbnail (at most 480 px wide).

attachments.description: Its screenshots, when it has any (get_attachment fetches one).

screen.description: Set on frames configured as screens for render checks: `status` (building: nodes under it are dirty; ready: built, no check for this design yet; requested; passed; mismatch; error), `stale` (the last result is for an older design) and the last `score` (% of pixels that differ).

notesResolved.description: `get_node` only: how many of its notes clears have resolved.

path.description: Ancestor node ids, root first, ending with this node.

descendants.description: Counts over the node's subtree, excluding the node itself (`include=counts`).

usage.description: Design tokens (`token:<variableKey>`) only: `layers` — how many live layers use the token (their captured `resolvedVariables` has an entry with its variable key, under any imported id). Always on `get_node`; on listings with `include=usage`.

via.description: Only with `expand=instances`: how the node was reached — `{ instanceId, mainComponentId, depth }` of the first (shortest) instance → main hop chain into its component; null for nodes in the original scope.

truncated.description: Present (true) when a change value on this page was replaced by `{ truncated: true, bytes }`.

expansion.description: Only with `expand=instances`: `components` — main components expanded; `truncated` — true when the 500-component limit stopped the expansion (then `hint` says how to narrow it); `unresolved` — main component ids instances point at that were never synced (sync their page to include them).

get.description: The file's activity log, oldest first: syncs, clears, claims, blocks (IDs, counts and labels, never design content). Use it to see what changed since you last looked, or who holds what. JSON page `{ events, nextAfter }`: poll with `after` = the previous `nextAfter`; `after=0` starts from the oldest retained event. After a `sync.completed`, re-read the affected nodes. To read the newest events first, pass `order=desc`: the page `{ events, nextBefore }` is newest first; pass `before` = the previous `nextBefore` for the next older page (omit `before` to start at the newest event). A page shorter than `limit` is the last one. Filters apply the same in both orders. Types: sync.completed, nodes.cleared, claim.created, claim.renewed, claim.released, node.blocked, node.unblocked, file.settings_changed, note.added, note.resolved, note.dismissed, render_check.requested, render_check.passed, render_check.mismatch. With `Accept: text/event-stream`: a server-sent-event stream. Each message has `id` (the event id), `event` (the type) and `data` (the event as JSON). It replays the events after `Last-Event-ID` (header, sent by EventSource on reconnect) or `?after=`, then streams live; without either it streams live only. A `: heartbeat` comment is sent every 20 s. When the requested id is older than the replay window (RDS_EVENT_REPLAY_HOURS), one `event: reset` is sent instead of the replay — re-fetch state — and the stream continues live. `format` applies to the JSON page only (`ndjson` / `md` stream every event after `after` — with order=desc, before `before`, newest first — up to `limit` when given). `nodeId` matches data.nodeId or a member of data.nodeIds in JSON and SSE. `since` is an inclusive ISO timestamp lower bound on JSON pages (ignored for SSE). Filters combine with types, after and before. `order` and `before` apply to JSON pages only (SSE is always oldest first).

get.description: The nodes the `list_nodes` filters match (default: dirty) bundled into work items — the best way to plan: fix a component once and its instances follow. Items are in document order (the design's layer order, by each item's key node), paged by `cursor`; each has its node ids (`claim_nodes` takes them), changed properties and categories. `group=component` (default): by the nearest COMPONENT / COMPONENT_SET ancestor-or-self; nodes with none form one item with `key: null`, listed last. Removed design (group=component and group=set): deleted nodes that were built are grouped under their removed root — the topmost deleted node — into one `kind: "removed"` item (after the component items, before `key: null`, in the roots' document order), unless that root sits inside a live component (then they are part of that component's item). For a removed item: remove the code that rendered the root; keep components in `uses` with `livePlacements > 0` (still used elsewhere), consider removing those with 0; heed `warnings`; then clear the root with `subtree: true` (`clear_nodes`) — one item clears the whole removed subtree. Deleted nodes that were never built are not work (they resolve at sync). Design tokens (group=component and group=set): the dirty tokens of each collection form one `kind: "tokens"` item (key = the collection node id, after the component and removed items, before `key: null`). For each token, update the code variable named by its `codeSyntax` (WEB, else the token name) for every changed `value:<Mode>`, then clear it. `include=usage` adds how many layers use each token. `group=set`: merge variants of each known component set into one item named like the Figma set, with its Figma key, set reference and variants [{ key, name, nodeCount }]. Use this to build a design system. Standalone components and variants whose set is unavailable keep their component item; the default grouping is unchanged. `group=frame`: by the ancestor one level below `under` (required); the `under` node itself is in the `key: null` item. `include=progress` adds { total, clean } for each returned item across all states, independent of state= and the nodeIds cap. Use clean / total for a progress bar. `expand=instances` answers "which components do I need to build for this screen, and how often does it use each?": with `under` = the screen, items also cover every main component its instances reach (transitively, each once; filters apply after expansion), and with `group=component` each item has `placementsInScope` beside the file-wide `placements`. Nodes of expanded components that are outside `under` fall in the `key: null` item with `group=frame`. Notes: a node someone noted as not matching the design is dirty with `changeType: requested` (category `note`) when its design is otherwise built, and grouped like any dirty node; `notes` counts an item's open notes. Read the notes (`get_node` or `list_notes`), fix the code to match the design as they describe, then clear the node — clearing resolves its notes. Each item's `changes` maps its listed node ids to their diffs (`changes=auto`: modified and deleted nodes; `diff`: added ones too; `names`: none — `changedProps` only). Values over 1 KB are `{ truncated: true, bytes }` and the page has `truncated: true`; `get_node` returns them whole.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Comma-separated: dirty, clean, blocked, requested, all. Default dirty (changed since last built or with open notes, not blocked); `requested`: dirty only by open notes; `all` for every state.

parameters.name: under
parameters.description: Only this node's subtree, the node included (1:2 or 1-2). Several subtrees: up to 50 comma-separated ids (1:2,1:5) for their union, each node once, in the order given. Defaults to the `url` link's node-id.

parameters.name: depth
parameters.description: Needs `under`: at most this many levels below it — below each root when there are several (1 = direct children).

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Comma-separated Figma node types, e.g. TEXT,INSTANCE,FRAME.

parameters.name: changeType
parameters.description: Comma-separated: added, modified, deleted, requested (dirty nodes only; `requested`: built as designed but with open notes).

parameters.name: changed
parameters.description: Comma-separated changed property names (fills, paddingLeft); a trailing `*` matches a prefix (padding*).

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Comma-separated change categories: layout, color, typography, effects, component, content, structure, prototype, token, other, note, render.

parameters.name: component
parameters.description: Comma-separated main component ids: the components and all their instances.

parameters.name: instance
parameters.description: true: only component instances (`isInstance`); false: only other nodes.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Comma-separated case-insensitive name globs (`*`, `?`), e.g. Button*.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: ISO 8601 time: only nodes changed at or after it.

parameters.name: claimed
parameters.description: Comma-separated: true (leased), false (free), mine (leased to `worker`).

parameters.name: worker
parameters.description: Your worker id; needed with `claimed=mine`.

parameters.name: library
parameters.description: Library nodes (remote main components / sets and their layers): include, exclude, or only them. Default: include when the file tracks library components (`settings.trackLibraryComponents`), else exclude.

parameters.name: hasNotes
parameters.description: true: only nodes with open notes; false: only nodes without.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: All the filters above in one string: space-separated `key:value` pairs, e.g. `state:dirty under:1:2 changed:fills` (several subtrees: `under:1:2,1:5`); quote values with spaces (name:"Primary Button"). A key may not also be passed as its own parameter.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: A Figma link (figma.com/design/<fileKey>/…?node-id=1-2). Supplies the path parameters given as '-'; on routes with `under`, its node-id is the default `under`.

parameters.name: expand
parameters.description: `instances`: also include the subtree of every main component the scope's instances use (the scope is `under`, or the whole file) — transitively through instances inside those components, breadth-first, each component once. Use it for "everything this screen uses" / "which components do I build for this screen". Other filters apply after expansion; `depth` cannot be combined with it.

parameters.name: expandDepth
parameters.description: With `expand=instances`: at most this many instance → main hops (default 10, max 20; 1 = only the components the scope uses directly).

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: component (default): by nearest component; set: merge all matching variants of a known component set (best for design systems); frame: by child frame of `under` (needs exactly one `under`).

parameters.name: changes
parameters.description: auto (default): each item's `changes` has the diffs of its modified and deleted nodes; diff: of every listed node, added ones included (their full values); names: no `changes`, only `changedProps`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Items per page (default 100, max 1000). With format=outline: rendered lines per page (default: every line).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The previous page's `nextCursor`, unchanged, with all other parameters the same (else `invalid_cursor`). With format=outline: the previous response's `X-RDS-Next-Cursor` header (a line position in the rendered outline).

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Comma-separated: progress, usage. progress: add total and clean node counts across all states for each work item; usage: add `usage: { nodeId: { layers } }` to token items.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: json (default); ndjson — one JSON object per line, streamed; md — a markdown checklist, one line per row, streamed. ndjson and md return every match from `cursor` on (up to `limit` when given) instead of one page. outline — text/plain, an indented tree with one line per item: use this first to see a screen's structure (under=<the screen>, and expand=instances for the components inside). Each item is a line `Name (TYPE) · 3 nodes · changed (4: characters, fills, …) · 2 placements`, with its listed nodes as an indented tree below it (`Name (TYPE) · modified (…)`, indented under their nearest listed ancestor). Lines are the `fields`-independent summary. The whole result (up to 2000 lines of whole items, in order) is rendered once, then paged by rendered lines, so nesting and `(shown above)` read the same at any page size: `limit` is lines per page (default: every line), and when lines remain the response has an `X-RDS-Next-Cursor` header — pass it as `cursor`, with every other parameter unchanged, for the next lines. Past the 2000-line cap the outline's last line (counted like any other) is `… N more items (use cursor/limit) — cursor=<c>` (the same cursor is in the header), which continues after the rendered part.

parameters.name: fileKey
parameters.description: The Figma file key, e.g. `AbCdEf123456` from figma.com/design/<fileKey>/… — not a URL. Pass '-' to take it from `url` instead.

kind.description: `removed`: design deleted in Figma that was built — one item per removed root (the topmost tombstoned node; key = its id), listing the components it used (`uses`). `library`: a reference item — a library (remote) main component the scope uses while the file does not track library components (`expand=instances`, group=component or set): `tracked: false`, `nodeCount: 0`, no `nodeIds`, no `progress`, with `placements` / `placementsInScope`. Use the library component as is; there is nothing to build or clear. `tokens`: design tokens of one collection (key = the collection node id `tokens:<collectionKey>`, name = the collection name; the `tokens` root's own changes have key `tokens`): for each changed `value:<Mode>` update the code variable named by the token's `codeSyntax` (WEB, else the token name) in that mode, then clear the tokens. Absent on other component, set and frame items.

tracked.description: Reference (`kind: "library"`) items only: false — the library component is not tracked in this file.

library.description: Items whose component is a library (remote) component: `{ key, fileKey?, resolved }` as on nodes. Absent on other items.

figmaUrl.description: Library items only: the component in its library file, or null while unresolved.

key.description: The component or frame node id; with group=set, the Figma set key (id when no key is available). Standalone components retain their node id; removed items: the removed root's id; null for nodes with none.

set.description: The variant's Figma component set. Omitted when unavailable (including inaccessible library parents).

variants.description: group=set only, when a set is known: its matching variants in document order. Counts cover the filtered nodes of each variant, not placements; the set root itself is not a variant.

key.description: Figma component key (node id when unavailable).

notes.description: Open notes on the listed `nodeIds`: read them on the nodes (`get_node` / `list_notes`), fix the code to match the design as they describe, then clear the nodes — clearing resolves them.

changes.description: `{ nodeId: { prop: { built, now, category } } }` for the listed `nodeIds` (per `changes=`: by default modified and deleted nodes only; absent with `changes=names`). A side over 1 KB is `{ truncated: true, bytes }`; `get_node` returns it whole.

placements.description: group=component: instance rows whose mainComponentId is the key.

placementsInScope.description: group=component with expand=instances: the instances of the key reached from the scope (inside `under` or inside the expanded components) — how often this screen uses it.

name.description: The main component's name; null when it was never synced.

set.description: The variant's Figma component set. Omitted when unavailable (including inaccessible library parents).

remote.description: True for a library (remote) main component, when captured.

placementsRemoved.description: Instance rows of it inside the removed subtree.

livePlacements.description: Live (not tombstoned) instance rows of it anywhere in the file. 0: nothing in the design uses it any more.

uses.description: Removed items only: the main components referenced by instances inside the removed subtree, those with `livePlacements: 0` first (then by name). Keep the code of components with livePlacements > 0; consider removing those with 0.

code.description: main_removed_with_live_placements: a main component inside the removed subtree still has live instances elsewhere — keep its code.

warnings.description: Removed items only (empty when none): main components removed with the design while other instances of them are still live.

screen.description: Items whose key is a screen root (group=frame per frame): its render-check state, as on the node.

usage.description: Token items with `include=usage`: `{ nodeId: { layers } }` for the listed tokens — how many live layers use each.

nodeIds.description: The item's first 50 node ids, in document order (the design's layer order; a removed item's root first).

more.description: How many node ids `nodeIds` leaves out.

progress.description: Present with include=progress: counts across all states for this item, independent of state=; other listing filters still apply. Cleared tombstones are excluded.

truncated.description: Present (true) when a change value on this page was replaced by `{ truncated: true, bytes }`.

expansion.description: Only with `expand=instances`: `components` — main components expanded; `truncated` — true when the 500-component limit stopped the expansion (then `hint` says how to narrow it); `unresolved` — main component ids instances point at that were never synced (sync their page to include them).

schema.description: A markdown checklist, one line per row.
An indented tree, one line per item (format=outline).

viewerToken.description: A read-only viewer token (RDS_VIEWER_TOKENS): GET routes only.

pluginToken.description: A plugin token (RDS_PLUGIN_TOKENS): the plugin routes (…/hashes, …/sync, …/exists) only.
